2607.09932.title: Faithful by Design: Evaluating and Improving LLM-Generated Clinical Trial Summaries for Multi-Stakeholder Audiences
2607.09932.paper_summary: Large language models are increasingly used to summarize clinical trial results for healthcare providers, patients, and payers, but their tendency to hallucinate poses significant risks in this high-stakes context. This study introduces a benchmark evaluation framework for measuring the faithfulness of LLM-generated clinical trial summaries across three stakeholder audiences. The framework consists of 200 stratified trials drawn from the Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov database, evaluated using audience-specific prompt templates and a six-dimension faithfulness annotation schema. Baseline measurements were established for GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 2.5 Flash across 1,800 generated summaries scored using a cross-encoder natural language inference (NLI) model. Unsupported Claims was identified as the dominant failure mode across all three models, with a mean annotation score of 1.55 out of three. A knowledge-graph-augmented retrieval system was developed and evaluated against the baseline, producing statistically significant improvements in NLI-based faithfulness scores (entailment +0.0125, faithfulness +0.0130, p < 0.0001). Improvement pathways were model-dependent, with GPT-4o improving primarily through contradiction reduction while Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Gemini 2.5 Flash improved through increased entailment.
2607.09932.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型越來越多地被用來為醫療提供者、患者和支付者總結臨床試驗結果，但它們的幻覺傾向在這個高風險的背景下帶來了重大風險。這項研究介紹了一個基準評估框架，用於衡量LLM生成的臨床試驗摘要在三個利益相關者群體中的忠實性。該框架由200個來自Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov數據庫的分層試驗組成，使用特定於受眾的提示模板和六維忠實性註釋架構進行評估。基準測量是在1,800個生成的摘要中為GPT-4o、Claude Sonnet 4.6和Gemini 2.5 Flash建立的，這些摘要使用交叉編碼器自然語言推理（NLI）模型進行評分。所有三個模型中，未支持的聲明被確定為主要的失敗模式，平均註釋分數為三分之1.55。開發了一個增強知識圖譜的檢索系統，並與基準進行了評估，產生了在基於NLI的忠實性分數上具有統計學意義的改善（包含 +0.0125，忠實性 +0.0130，p < 0.0001）。改善路徑依賴於模型，GPT-4o主要通過減少矛盾來改善，而Claude Sonnet 4.6和Gemini 2.5 Flash則通過增加包含關係來改善。
